criterion.title: Bounded protocol overhead for sporadic communication
criterion.definition: After 24 hours with the endpoint radio silent, exchange 256 useful bytes with one previously authorized peer. Retain provisioned identity, configuration and valid trust, but expire sessions and learned neighbor state. The budget is 65,536 bytes total endpoint-interface transmit plus receive, including selected-stack control, discovery, fresh establishment, framing and useful data, through delivery. Assume no losses and one hop to access. Infrastructure is available; its traffic not crossing this endpoint interface is outside this metric. This is a bounded documentary configuration witness, not an energy measurement, global traffic bound or guarantee for every configuration.
criterion.research_action: Count all endpoint-facing traffic for a complete selected-stack witness; preserve unresolved components explicitly.

cells.reason: The selected column still specifies wire-v4 with protected adjacency and E2E suite 0x0202. The effective wire-v4 document retains ONION and two-flight HS2. The author-approved no-ONION fast-path direction belongs to a separately described successor: the TPA proposal explicitly preserves the existing wire implementation and leaves successor encoding/migration unqualified. These are not interchangeable byte budgets. Rechecking legacy TLV widths for identity suite 0x0002 gives M1=1736 and M2=1778 bytes; two fresh exchanges total 7028 canonical HS2 bytes before framing. For 256 useful bytes split into two 128-byte directions, legacy OPEN/ACCEPT plus four E2E item headers, four RRL record headers and four list counts total 384 inner bytes. The older 640-byte candidate instead contained 512 useful bytes. Neither inner amount is a complete endpoint budget or automatically additive to historical link subtotals. The next source review locates an actual cover scheduler and padding policy: prp_session_cover_work_fn sends an empty two-byte RRL only for active adjacent TX sessions. For suite 0x0202 the unpadded protected unit is 30 bytes (12 nonce + 2 RRL + 16 tag). Its size is raised to the configured padding target, bounded by session capacity. The scheduler uses ceil(8*unit_bytes*10^9/cover_rate_bps) nanoseconds with a 1 ms floor, and schedules from the actual current time rather than replaying missed intervals. At a 256-byte target and 1024 bit/s, one stable TX adjacency sends at most 1+floor(T/2 seconds) automatic cover units over an active interval T. For one such adjacency in each direction and T=60 seconds, the conservative cover-only bound is 18228 native Ethernet byte-times or 19964 over IPv4/UDP/Ethernet. This is a conditional source-derived bound, not measured completion in 60 seconds. Native Ethernet discovery now has a concrete source witness: version 2 SOLICIT and ANNOUNCE payloads are 48 bytes. A received SOLICIT causes a unicast ANNOUNCE when the link is allowed; ANNOUNCE records TX_ADDRESSABLE and RX_OBSERVED with current member generation and lease. One bilateral discovery cycle has two solicitations and two responses, totaling 344 untagged Ethernet byte-times (4*(48+38)). The default scan interval is 10000 ms and advertised lease 30000 ms. On an isolated two-node link, starting with no queued discovery work, no manual solicitations, resets or withdrawals, a 60-second interval has at most 28 such frames under a schedule with spacing at least ten seconds: 2408 byte-times. This accounts for continuing periodic discovery, not just the initial exchange.
cells.method: Native carrier source trace and conditional discovery-frame bound; no runtime execution
cells.source_label: Effective sibling specification files pinned by path and SHA256 in round474-sources.json; successor files include uncommitted proposals, not all attributable to the observed HEAD or public mirror
cells.qualification: Native discovery is source-bound, not an unbounded unknown or a zero-cost assumption. The interval calculation assumes stable allowed attachments, one interface per node, no other discovery participants/traffic and at least 10-second actual scan spacing; a Linux timing realization must preserve that spacing. Local current-member context creation remains necessary after wake; a carrier ANNOUNCE proves no PRP identity and HS2 still authenticates the peer. The 60-second interval is not an execution result or guaranteed delivery time. The complete F25 sequence still needs actual admission, route/relation exchange multiplicity, protected useful-data wrapping and successful delivery time consistent with the positive cover policy from round475. No independent acceptance of integration or the no-ONION successor is inferred. This Ethernet-discovery count is not silently reused for the UDP/IP carrier.

cells.qualification: F25 remains Pending. The cover-rate field is not a total interface shaper: real traffic is additional, and the separate TX_CREDIT path can emit extra cover units. The candidate therefore excludes manual credit requests, cover-policy resets and replacement adjacencies during its measured interval, with exactly one active TX adjacency in each direction and capacity at least 256 bytes. Ethernet is untagged; IPv4 has no options; 38 Ethernet byte-times and 28 IPv4/UDP bytes are counted per 256-byte unit. PHY-specific coding is not included. Target=256 is a padding floor, not a cap on larger real packets. The 60-second duration is an explicit candidate condition still needing a successful complete sequence, not a newly imposed F25 deadline. Actual bootstrap, route/relation controls, protected data wrapping and delivery time remain to be bounded together. Local admission method 0 permits direct HS2 without challenge/proof while retaining 0x0202; it is not a downgrade or a universal entitlement against a peer requiring PoW. The no-ONION successor is not substituted. No source binding here claims integrated implementation acceptance.

cells.reason: Constructive IPv4/Ethernet witness: retained static numeric addressing and route, expired ARP cache, no options, no session or added transport. A successful ARP request/reply costs 2 x 84 byte-times including minimum-frame padding, preamble and inter-frame gap. Two datagrams each carrying 256 useful bytes cost 2 x (256 + 20 + 38). Total 796, below 65,536. This even allows 256 useful bytes in each direction. Cold neighbor acquisition and recurring wake use the same exchange.

cells.reason: A controlled short-contact witness completes the earlier LTP/AOS inventory. Charge 1,024 acquisition octets and 24 complete 1,028-octet AOS-plus-ASM units in each direction: 51,392 bytes total, below 65,536. The 48 units include twelve data/report/ack units and 36 idle units. Four initial idle units establish fresh frame synchronization; data occupy slots 5-8, reports slot 10 and acknowledgments slot 12. At one frame per second, <=0.1 s one-way propagation and <=0.1 s response processing leave causal guards and avoid a 20 s retransmission timer. A complete 256-byte useful payload is carried each way in the compact protected BP bundle; no application fragmentation assumption is needed.
cells.method: Conditional documentary byte bound and executable timing arithmetic; no RF or full-stack execution
cells.source_label: Primary LTP/AOS/Encapsulation and synchronization formats; explicit constructed short-contact schedule
cells.qualification: Yes is a bounded documentary plausibility result, not measured performance or a universal spacecraft-link bound. The constructed receiver must acquire within the explicitly charged 1,024-octet prefix and four initial idle frames; CCSDS does not guarantee that acquisition time. Provisioned short, loss-free links, rates/clocks, engine/channel mappings, contact plans and valid BPSec keys are retained after 24 h silence; LTP sessions and frame synchronization are fresh. All idle traffic through the scheduled stop is counted. Pin uncoded historical 131.0-B-3, mandatory FECF inside each 1,024-byte AOS frame, compact managed options and Encapsulation fill. No other traffic, reports, coding, retries or plan/key downloads. Longer acquisition, propagation or processing requires recalculation. Full BPv7/BPSec/LTP/Encapsulation/AOS executable integration and physical receiver validation remain unqualified; this decision does not resolve E03, D03, G05 or security testing.

Compact certificate <=2,048 bytes and each Identify response <=1,024 bytes, small configured address/protocol metadata, first protocol accepted, sufficient stream/flow credit, bounded packetization and timely loss-free exchange. Optional services such as DHT, NAT discovery, relay and pubsub are not part of this selected known-peer profile. TLS suite choice here is a size witness, not a K01 resolution.

cells.reason: Tor client-operation permits use of a consensus that expired less than 24 hours ago when no live consensus is available. Therefore 24 hours of radio silence does not itself imply that this tolerance has elapsed: a consensus with two hours of validity left at shutdown is only 22 hours past expiry on return. Clients can select microdescriptor consensuses and retain cached descriptors. Separately, directory mirrors support consensus diffs from a known consensus; directory compression includes deflate and recommended LZMA for consensuses and diffs. The size of an uncompressed full consensus is consequently not a mandatory endpoint transfer lower bound for this workload. Four public CollecTor microdescriptor consensuses, valid-after 10:00 UTC on 19–22 October 2026, were downloaded and hashed. Local XZ preset-6 compression of full documents produced 677460–690468 bytes. GNU ed-style differences between consecutive daily documents, compressed with the same setting, produced 62348, 77212 and 79548 bytes. Applying each uncompressed difference reconstructed the next document exactly. Only the first diagnostic difference fits within 65536 bytes, leaving 3188 bytes before any other traffic. Deflate level 9 produced 74814, 91308 and 92984 bytes for the same differences. These are measured document transformations, not a Tor endpoint capture or mirror response. Source inspection of Tor tag tor-0.4.8.16 separates cached-consensus usability from refresh scheduling. networkstatus_consensus_is_bootstrapping returns false for a validated reasonably-live consensus. However, update_consensus_networkstatus_downloads sets the next fetch time to now whenever the consensus is outside its strict validity interval, then checks outstanding requests, retry readiness and missing certificates before requesting a fresh consensus. fetch_networkstatus_callback checks normally every 60 seconds, or every second during the specified testing or bootstrap cases. This interval is not a guaranteed grace period after wake. The reasonably-live predicate in this version includes the exact 24-hour expiry boundary. DisableNetwork delays fetches but also closes outbound connections, so it does not provide directory-only suppression while useful traffic continues.
cells.method: Source control-flow trace of usability, scheduling and disable-network behavior
cells.source_label: Tor tor-0.4.8.16 networkstatus.c, mainloop.c and manual; SHA-256 pins
cells.qualification: F25-TO remains Pending. Cache usability does not establish zero refresh traffic. The inspected scheduler does not establish that a complete refresh necessarily finishes before useful delivery either. Do not charge an entire response solely from a scheduled request. The remaining witness must specify retained directory material, loop phase and request state, and count endpoint bytes actually required through delivery, including fresh connections, onion-service lookup and rendezvous. Round436 local GNU-diff compression is not the actual Tor response. This is a version-bounded source trace, not execution of Tor or a statement about every implementation. No criterion or profile change is made.

cells.reason: A bounded configuration witness fits the 65,536-byte F25 budget. Three fresh Yggdrasil v0.5.14 / Ironwood d50055b runs deliver and byte-verify 256 useful bytes in each direction using the ordinary numeric IPv6/UDP API, pinned numeric TLS peering and independent Ed25519 keys. Linux TCP_INFO on the endpoint-facing relay socket reports stream-byte totals 7,385/7,361/7,123 and combined incoming/outgoing segment counts 44/42/38, with no retransmissions, unacknowledged or unsent data at the snapshot. TCP_MAXSEG=1200 yields measured send/receive MSS 1188. Map each trace to provisioned IPv4, untagged Ethernet MTU 1500, no losses, no DHCP/DNS or multicast peer discovery, and fresh ARP. Charge 20 IPv4 + 60 maximum TCP-header + 38 Ethernet byte-times per counted segment, add three complete handshake segments conservatively for listener counter omissions, and two 84-byte-time ARP frames. Totals are 13,099 / 12,839 / 12,129 byte-times, including startup, routing convergence, session establishment and both complete useful payloads. The largest is below 65,536.
cells.method: Measured TCP stream and segment accounting plus a conditional loss-free Ethernet configuration model
cells.source_label: Pinned upstream code; three ordinary-path successful local executions; Linux TCP_INFO counters and explicit Ethernet/ARP accounting
cells.qualification: Yes is a documentary low-latency single-peer configuration witness, not a physical Ethernet capture or universal upper bound. Actual execution is loopback; TCP bytes and segment counts are measured, while Ethernet/ARP and transfer of the observed loss-free packetization to the specified link are modeled. The opposite TCP relay leg is infrastructure outside the endpoint interface; the relay does not terminate TLS. Fresh cores stand in for retained valid keys/configuration with expired sessions/learned state, not a physical 24-hour sleep. Payload verification and a 300 ms settling window precede the snapshot; teardown after delivery is outside F25. The upstream routing-readiness wait plus three-second settling delay is not a convergence guarantee. A slower link, other peers, loss/retransmission, background traffic, dynamic addressing, VLAN/Wi-Fi, or different packetization needs a new budget. This credits no energy, global capacity, or runtime interoperability certification.

cells.reason: A bounded fresh mutually authenticated QUIC/TLS1.3 exchange plus multipath-21 setup fits the F25 budget with two validated paths. Reserve 16 crypto/handshake datagrams, eight CID/path-control datagrams, four proactively duplicated STREAM datagrams, two closes and four extra padded Initial ACK datagrams, each with UDP payload up to 1,232 bytes. Add 28 small ACK/PATH_ACK-only datagrams and eight ARP frames across both access interfaces. Including IPv4/UDP and Ethernet overhead, the total is at most 50,236 byte-times. Mandatory 1,200-byte Initial/path-probe padding is included. This retained positive witness uses IPv4 only; the exact total is not an IPv6 overhead calculation.

cells.qualification: Compact local certificate chains <=2,048 bytes, bounded Hello/transport parameters, two paths, CID <=20 bytes, single-range ACKs and no loss, Retry, version negotiation, ticket/resumption, 0-RTT or key update. Additional Initial-ACK padding is explicitly budgeted; the small-ACK bound does not apply to Initial packets requiring padding. Configure timely acknowledgments and no unrelated PING/rotation/traffic before delivery. Optional proactive copies are counted on both paths. This is one allowed TLS-suite/packetization witness, not a change to K01 or a general certificate/profile bound. No runtime, congestion, energy or interoperability qualification.

cells.reason: A same-AS SCION/UDP endpoint exchange fits the 64 KiB budget with fresh underlay neighbor discovery. The official Empty path has zero wire bytes and is valid inside an AS. Pinned v0.13.0 snet writer code derives the direct underlay next hop from the numeric destination when the local and remote IAs match. With IPv4 host addresses, the SCION header is 12 common + 24 address + 0 path bytes. Each 256-byte UDP payload therefore costs 366 Ethernet byte-times including both UDP headers, outer IPv4 and link overhead. Two directions plus a fresh ARP request/reply total 900 byte-times. No expiring inter-AS segment or transport session is reused.
cells.method: Constructive same-AS documentary byte envelope; no new protocol execution
cells.source_label: Versioned official SCION header specification and v0.13.0 packet construction, plus IPv4/ARP/Ethernet accounting
cells.qualification: Conditional intra-AS witness, not a bound for Internet-wide SCION, remote path retrieval or control-plane startup. Use two endpoints in one provisioned IPv4/Ethernet subnet, numeric addresses, retained local topology/IA/ports and valid trust, with local daemon/dispatcher access. Expire neighbor state; count both ARP frames. No loss, unrelated broadcasts, optional extensions, DHCP/DNS, VLAN, fragmentation or extra security layer. This column supplies no end-to-end TLS or cryptographic peer authentication; none is inferred from the small budget. Any cross-AS, remote-daemon, certificate-refresh or additional link-security configuration needs a separate inventory. The established F25 definition accepts one bounded configuration and does not require crossing AS boundaries. No packet capture, implementation certification or energy claim.

cells.reason: Reticulum 1.5.5 supports a configured serial witness with retained identity/IFAC credentials and an expired Link/path cache. The adjacent available peer hosts the known destination. Eight endpoint packets cover path request, path-response announce, Link request, Link proof, RTT confirmation, Link.identify, a 256-byte encrypted data packet and explicit delivery proof. Each is bounded by the 500-byte selected Link MTU, plus a configured 16-byte IFAC. Worst-case HDLC escaping and two flags cost at most 1,034 serial octets per packet: 8,272 total. Charging 8N1 start/stop bits and rounding upward per packet gives 10,344 byte-equivalents, below 65,536.

cells.qualification: Bounded documentary witness, not a measurement or a bound for a busy mesh. Use one serial interface at 115200 8N1, Link MTU 500 (disable link MTU discovery), IFAC 128 bits, empty announce application data, no unrelated announced destinations, no probe service or periodic application announcements. The path-response context does not require ordinary announce rebroadcast. Retain provisioned keys and authorization; perform a fresh Link and identify before data acceptance. Deliver promptly before retry/keepalive timers; no claims about CPU time or energy. No Resource/LXMF transfer is added. This does not settle global announce volume, F15 or G05.

cells.reason: The selected Router.cpp supplies a concrete small-message candidate. For a direct PKI message with portnum 1, 128 useful payload bytes, explicit zero bitfield and other optional Data fields unset, protobuf encoding occupies 135 bytes: 2 for portnum, 3+128 for payload and 2 for bitfield. Adding the 16-byte Meshtastic header and 12-byte PKI overhead yields 163 bytes, below 255. perhapsEncode signs normal broadcasts rather than ordinary PKI unicasts; checkXeddsaReceivePolicy explicitly accepts the successfully decoded pki_encrypted branch even under STRICT without an additional XEdDSA signature. Two such messages would carry 256 useful bytes with a 326-byte radio-packet subtotal.

cells.reason: The GNUnet 0.20.0 CADET wire inventory now distinguishes connection creation, authenticated tunnel key exchange, channel opening and useful data. ConnectionCreate includes a connection ID, monotime fields/signature and the whole peer path; the connection source sets/signs monotime in the applicable creation branch. TunnelKeyExchange carries ephemeral and ratchet public keys; TunnelKeyExchangeAuth additionally carries a KDF proof. ChannelOpen and its acknowledgement are separate structures, followed by application data and optional reliable-delivery acknowledgements inside encrypted tunnel messages. The legacy UDP plugin adds its own message header, reserved field and sender identity, and has fragmentation machinery. Additional lower-layer controls are now located in the selected release. Legacy TRANSPORT validation uses a challenge PING and a signed PONG with expiration and a variable address suffix. CORE send_key explicitly sends ephemeral key material plus an encrypted PING, with a PONG response path. Its initial key retry interval is ten seconds and periodic rekey interval twelve hours. CORE EncryptedMessage adds its own header, IV seed, full hash MAC, sequence/reserved fields and timestamp around higher-layer traffic. These cannot be omitted from a CADET-only packet inventory.

cells.qualification: Count the executed message sequence, not just one key-exchange header. Verify message multiplicity and timer conditions in the chosen no-loss configuration before comparing with 65,536 bytes. Do not substitute newer TNG/AEAD message layouts for the selected 0.20.0 legacy UDP profile. No measured or complete documentary bound yet; F25 remains Pending. Include the discovered TRANSPORT PING/PONG and CORE key/PING/PONG exchanges, CORE message-type advertisement/confirmation, and the variable transport-address suffix. Verify retry timing against actual successful establishment; the 24-hour silence must not reuse a CORE session simply because identity keys are retained. The located timer values and structures are source evidence, not a completion-time or total-byte bound.

cells.reason: The already selected private direct-serial role admits a bounded wake-up witness. Count fresh AX.25 and NET/ROM connection setup, four data frames for one message in each direction, transport and link acknowledgments, two small announcements and conservative shutdown/maintenance reserves: 32 frames total. A generous 512-byte frame cap, KISS command byte, worst-case doubling by escaping, delimiters and 8N1 start/stop bits yield 41,120 byte-equivalents, below 65,536.

cells.qualification: Constructive documentary direct-serial configuration, not a runtime measurement or radio-airtime bound.
